Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)

Before coding, state a compact visible-image specification: major silhouettes and
normalized bounds (top-left origin), architectural boundary endpoints, perspective
line directions, foreground cropping, and occlusion order. Distinguish observations
from uncertain depth assumptions. Name camera position, target, lens and major object
dimensions as parameters. Build all substantial visible objects on the first attempt.
Match the visible negative spaces as carefully as occupied regions: openings between
supports, under furniture, around foreground objects and through the room.

Keep construction economical. SceneAct sweep_tube emits a sphere at every point and
one cylinder per segment; fillet_box emits many separate meshes. Long decorative
loops and floor grids can create thousands of objects before rendering even begins.
Use boxes for flat parts, rods for straight parts, and short sweeps for curved outlines.
Restrict repeated geometry to visible regions. Use procedural material patterns for
fine surface markings, never the input image. Avoid modeling subpixel stitches, grain,

without omitting important objects. Simplify detail further when time is short.

Check source before returning every program:
- fillet_box requires 0 < radius <= half the smallest size component.
- rod endpoints are keyword arguments and must be distinct. Consecutive sweep points

- include replaces a child with the same key; include every loop index in repeated keys.
- Transform pivots default to bounding-box centers; specify other pivots explicitly.
- realize clears Blender. Create camera, lights and material customization afterward.
  Obtain bpy.context.scene after realize. Create its world if None and enable use_nodes

  target mesh descendants of the relevant marker and copy shared materials for local edits.
- Keep all visible parts of an object under its meaningful assembly through revisions.

After rendering, compare actual images, not the intended effect of code. Use a small
residual table: region or landmark, reference estimate, rendered estimate, discrepancy,
likely cause, and proposed parameter change. Estimates are visual, not measurements.
Check architecture and foreground together before changing the camera. Global position
errors suggest aim/shift; slopes suggest orientation; near/far ratios suggest camera
position and lens. Local errors suggest geometry or placement. Explain any coupled
camera and geometry change. Prioritize silhouette, occlusion, framing, large color
regions and illumination over ornament. Avoid simultaneously darkening every material
and reducing all lights: isolate the dominant cause of a brightness discrepancy.
Do not infer hidden objects or exact physical dimensions from category conventions.

Observed bounds use normalized image coordinates, with the origin at top left. The brown desktop fills roughly (0.00, 0.49)–(1.00, 1.00). A blue monitor occupies (0.02, 0.03)–(0.35, 0.45); an oscilloscope sits below it at (0.21, 0.40)–(0.46, 0.59). Wall drawer cabinets span (0.44, 0.00)–(1.00, 0.27). The long black lamp crosses (0.49, 0.16)–(0.85, 0.29). Major tabletop objects are a keyboard, two yellow meters, power supplies, a soldering station, calculator, circuit boards, probes, and tangled cables.

The wall/desk boundary runs approximately from (0.00, 0.66) to (1.00, 0.49), interrupted by equipment. Desk depth lines converge upward; cabinet edges are nearly horizontal. The desktop and right tool packaging are cropped by the bottom and right borders. Foreground wires overlap the keyboard and meters; instruments obscure the rear desktop; the lamp overlaps wall papers and cabinets. Exact depths are uncertain: the program assumes a shallow workbench against one wall.

Parameters below name the camera position, target, lens, bench dimensions, and major equipment dimensions. Fine labels are simplified. Source checks: positive dimensions, valid distinct rod endpoints, unique repeated keys, short cable sweeps, and camera/material setup after `realize`.

from sceneact import *
import bpy
import math
import random

random.seed(19)
scene = Scene("Electronics workbench")

CAMERA_POSITION = (0.48, -2.75, 2.34)
CAMERA_TARGET = (0.0, 0.13, 1.03)
CAMERA_LENS = 45
BENCH_SIZE = (2.18, 1.40, 0.07)
MONITOR_SIZE = (0.70, 0.055, 0.51)
SCOPE_SIZE = (0.53, 0.30, 0.28)

wood = (0.34, 0.19, 0.12)
black = (0.018, 0.023, 0.024)
dark = (0.055, 0.065, 0.064)
gray = (0.45, 0.47, 0.43)
cream = (0.66, 0.68, 0.57)
silver = (0.57, 0.60, 0.57)
red = (0.63, 0.025, 0.018)
yellow = (0.94, 0.59, 0.018)
paper = (0.82, 0.82, 0.73)

def asset(name):
    a = Asset(name)
    scene.include(name, a)
    return a

def B(a, name, size, center, color):
    a.include(name, box(size=size, center=center, color=color))

def R(a, name, radius, start, end, color):
    a.include(name, rod(radius=radius, start=start, end=end, color=color))

def S(a, name, points, radius, color):
    a.include(name, sweep_tube(points=points, radius=radius, color=color))

bench = asset("brown workbench")
B(bench, "laminated top", BENCH_SIZE, (0, -0.02, 0.705), wood)
B(bench, "front edge", (2.18, 0.035, 0.065), (0, -0.713, 0.70), (0.24, .13, .08))
wall = asset("rear wall")
B(wall, "plaster", (3.1, .07, 2.8), (0, .735, 1.30), (.54, .54, .46))
B(wall, "left return", (.06, 1.7, 2.5), (-1.17, .1, 1.3), (.43, .44, .38))

# Wall storage, with distinct recessed drawer fronts and pale labels.
for ci, (cx, width, rows, cols, cz) in enumerate([
    (-.02, .56, 4, 4, 1.86),
    (.70, .82, 5, 5, 1.84)
]):
    a = asset("parts cabinet %d" % ci)
    height = .44 if ci == 0 else .52
    B(a, "outer case", (width, .16, height), (cx, .64, cz), black)
    cw = (width-.035)/cols
    ch = (height-.025)/rows
    for row in range(rows):
        for col in range(cols):
            x = cx-width/2+.018+cw*(col+.5)
            z = cz-height/2+.012+ch*(row+.5)
            k = "%d_%d" % (row,col)
            B(a, "drawer "+k, (cw-.009,.013,ch-.009),
              (x,.548,z), (.18,.21,.20))
            B(a, "label "+k, (cw*.55,.004,ch*.24),
              (x,.539,z-ch*.18), (.60,.62,.56))
            B(a, "pull "+k, (cw*.27,.017,.008),
              (x,.53,z+ch*.12), (.10,.12,.12))

papers = asset("wall paperwork")
for i,(x,z,w,h) in enumerate([
    (-.12,1.40,.45,.28),(.31,1.38,.37,.31),(.70,1.35,.38,.30)
]):
    B(papers,"sheet%d"%i,(w,.006,h),(x,.691,z),paper)
    for j in range(5):
        B(papers,"writing%d_%d"%(i,j),(w*.65,.002,.002),
          (x,.686,z+.07-j*.023),(.56,.57,.53))

# Computer monitor: blue inset face and a modest desktop stand.
monitor = asset("computer monitor")
mx,my,mz = -.74,.41,1.40
B(monitor,"black housing",MONITOR_SIZE,(mx,my,mz),black)
B(monitor,"blue screen",(.638,.006,.435),(mx,my-.031,mz+.006),(.025,.35,.78))
B(monitor,"task bar",(.638,.003,.018),(mx,my-.036,mz-.201),(.015,.18,.57))
B(monitor,"top screen highlight",(.638,.003,.023),(mx,my-.036,mz+.211),(.04,.48,.94))
B(monitor,"login box",(.047,.003,.023),(mx+.02,my-.037,mz-.004),(.62,.72,.77))
B(monitor,"login stripe",(.011,.002,.018),(mx+.015,my-.039,mz-.004),(.82,.13,.08))
B(monitor,"login caption",(.12,.002,.003),(mx,my-.039,mz-.035),(.58,.76,.87))
R(monitor,"neck",.026,(mx,.43,.79),(mx,.43,1.15),black)
B(monitor,"foot",(.30,.19,.024),(mx,.39,.761),black)

# Benchtop power supply at the left.
supply = asset("left bench power supply")
B(supply,"case",(.25,.26,.30),(-.91,.24,.91),(.40,.43,.35))
B(supply,"front panel",(.24,.012,.27),(-.91,.104,.91),cream)
B(supply,"display",(.15,.008,.063),(-.91,.094,.98),(.13,.19,.15))
for i in range(3):
    R(supply,"knob%d"%i,.021,(-.98+i*.064,.09,.865),(-.98+i*.064,.063,.865),gray)
for i in range(2):
    R(supply,"socket%d"%i,.010,(-.96+i*.085,.088,.80),(-.96+i*.085,.066,.80),
      red if i else black)

scope = asset("oscilloscope")
B(scope,"case",SCOPE_SIZE,(-.51,.31,.925),cream)
B(scope,"front",(.515,.015,.255),(-.51,.151,.925),(.68,.70,.62))
B(scope,"screen surround",(.275,.018,.208),(-.61,.137,.933),(.36,.40,.35))
B(scope,"dark glass",(.239,.005,.174),(-.61,.124,.933),(.075,.11,.10))
for i in range(5):
    B(scope,"screen grid v%d"%i,(.001,.002,.161),(-.71+i*.05,.120,.933),(.13,.18,.15))
for i in range(4):
    B(scope,"screen grid h%d"%i,(.228,.002,.001),(-.61,.120,.872+i*.04),(.13,.18,.15))
for row in range(3):
    for col in range(3):
        R(scope,"control%d_%d"%(row,col),.014,
          (-.42+col*.052,.133,.859+row*.062),
          (-.42+col*.052,.104,.859+row*.062),(.58,.60,.53))
for i in range(5):
    B(scope,"top switch%d"%i,(.024,.012,.009),(-.44+i*.034,.128,1.033),gray)
for x in (-.70,-.32):
    B(scope,"foot%.2f"%x,(.05,.12,.02),(x,.31,.775),black)

rear = asset("rear black power box")
B(rear,"body",(.34,.24,.12),(-.12,.38,.82),black)
B(rear,"front stripe",(.32,.008,.035),(-.12,.255,.817),(.07,.08,.07))
for i in range(4):
    R(rear,"terminal%d"%i,.013,(-.24+i*.08,.249,.816),
      (-.24+i*.08,.226,.816),yellow if i==0 else red if i==3 else silver)
for i in range(2):
    B(rear,"coiled item%d"%i,(.10,.11,.035),(-.20+i*.12,.40,.905),(.12,.17,.21))
S(rear,"top lead",[(-.29,.39,.93),(-.31,.48,.95),(-.17,.51,.94),(-.08,.44,.93)],.006,silver)

# Upright yellow multimeter; local geometry tilted back as a unit.
meter = asset("upright yellow multimeter")
B(meter,"yellow shell",(.17,.058,.315),(.26,.30,.948),yellow)
B(meter,"dark face",(.141,.007,.279),(.26,.267,.949),(.18,.21,.19))
B(meter,"LCD",(.115,.004,.065),(.26,.262,1.038),(.40,.48,.38))
for i in range(3):
    B(meter,"LCD segment%d"%i,(.018,.002,.028),(.225+i*.033,.258,1.037),(.19,.25,.20))
R(meter,"selector",.037,(.26,.258,.925),(.26,.246,.925),black)
R(meter,"selector pointer",.006,(.26,.239,.925),(.281,.239,.942),gray)
for i in range(3):
    R(meter,"input%d"%i,.009,(.215+i*.044,.258,.831),(.215+i*.044,.243,.831),black)
meter.turn(axis="+x",degrees=-10,pivot=(.26,.30,.79))

small = asset("small foreground meter")
B(small,"yellow rim",(.132,.21,.039),(.21,-.19,.774),yellow)
B(small,"face",(.112,.188,.008),(.21,-.19,.798),black)
B(small,"display",(.085,.05,.004),(.21,-.133,.805),(.42,.48,.39))
R(small,"dial",.029,(.21,-.207,.803),(.21,-.207,.817),(.23,.26,.24))
for i in range(2):
    R(small,"jack%d"%i,.009,(.183+i*.052,-.268,.805),(.183+i*.052,-.268,.816),red if i else black)
small.turn(axis="+z",degrees=-12)

keyboard = asset("keyboard")
B(keyboard,"body",(.79,.285,.032),(-.48,-.285,.765),black)
for row in range(5):
    for col in range(15):
        if row == 0 and 4 <= col <= 9:
            continue
        B(keyboard,"key%d_%d"%(row,col),(.041,.039,.012),
          (-.835+col*.049,-.391+row*.050,.787),(.045,.05,.048))
B(keyboard,"space",(.26,.036,.012),(-.49,-.391,.787),(.055,.06,.058))
keyboard.turn(axis="+z",degrees=13)

calculator = asset("calculator")
B(calculator,"body",(.18,.28,.035),(-.94,-.53,.769),(.075,.09,.085))
B(calculator,"LCD",(.142,.061,.005),(-.94,-.45,.791),(.42,.48,.41))
for row in range(5):
    for col in range(4):
        B(calculator,"button%d_%d"%(row,col),(.030,.025,.009),
          (-.999+col*.039,-.49-row*.035,.792),(.53,.55,.49))
calculator.turn(axis="+z",degrees=14)

board = asset("exposed circuit board")
B(board,"blue pcb",(.22,.15,.014),(-.62,.035,.756),(.018,.14,.38))
for i in range(5):
    B(board,"chip%d"%i,(.025,.035,.014),(-.70+i*.036,.032,.77),black)
for i in range(6):
    R(board,"capacitor%d"%i,.009,(-.69+i*.032,.083,.765),
      (-.69+i*.032,.083,.789),silver)
board.turn(axis="+z",degrees=15)

# Large articulated black bench lamp.
lamp = asset("black task lamp")
B(lamp,"clamp",(.08,.09,.11),(.91,.49,.80),black)
R(lamp,"lower arm",.014,(.91,.49,.83),(.78,.49,1.19),black)
R(lamp,"upper arm",.014,(.78,.49,1.19),(.76,.48,1.66),black)
R(lamp,"parallel arm",.009,(.81,.49,1.20),(.79,.48,1.65),silver)
R(lamp,"hinge",.032,(.75,.455,1.64),(.75,.505,1.64),black)
B(lamp,"long shade",(.64,.185,.065),(.39,.43,1.67),black)
B(lamp,"end housing",(.14,.17,.072),(.76,.43,1.66),black)
B(lamp,"underside diffuser",(.54,.14,.007),(.37,.43,1.633),(.72,.73,.64))
B(lamp,"small switch",(.035,.05,.008),(.15,.43,1.707),silver)
S(lamp,"power cord",[(.77,.48,1.63),(.86,.51,1.49),(.83,.49,1.22),(.94,.48,.93),(.91,.35,.76)],.006,black)

# Soldering station, stand, metal spring and iron.
station = asset("soldering equipment")
B(station,"base",(.26,.23,.09),(.79,.24,.79),(.12,.15,.15))
B(station,"sloped panel",(.23,.018,.075),(.79,.115,.825),(.30,.33,.29))
R(station,"temperature knob",.025,(.83,.098,.83),(.83,.076,.83),black)
B(station,"iron stand foot",(.21,.18,.023),(.76,-.06,.756),(.18,.19,.17))
R(station,"stand upright",.013,(.77,-.035,.77),(.84,.015,.94),silver)
for i in range(8):
    # Economical eight visible rings, each using four short segments.
    x=.82+i*.012
    pts=[(x,.005+.035*math.cos(t),.941+.035*math.sin(t))
         for t in (0,math.pi/2,math.pi,3*math.pi/2,2*math.pi)]
    S(station,"spring%d"%i,pts,.005,(.25,.28,.27))
R(station,"iron grip",.024,(.87,.07,.97),(.94,.24,1.04),(.025,.20,.22))
R(station,"iron collar",.026,(.86,.05,.962),(.88,.09,.978),silver)
R(station,"iron shaft",.007,(.78,-.13,.89),(.86,.05,.962),silver)
S(station,"iron cord",[(.94,.24,1.04),(1.01,.30,1.01),(1.04,.19,.85),(.98,-.10,.75),(.71,-.30,.75)],.009,black)

cans = asset("rear cans and bottle")
for i,(x,y,h,r) in enumerate([(.61,.47,.23,.041),(.74,.51,.20,.038)]):
    R(cans,"can%d"%i,r,(x,y,.745),(x,y,.745+h),silver)
    B(cans,"dark label%d"%i,(r*1.7,.008,h*.48),(x,y-r,.745+h*.49),(.18,.23,.19))
    R(cans,"cap%d"%i,r*.76,(x,y,.745+h),(x,y,.755+h),gray)
R(cans,"water bottle",.045,(1.00,.56,.76),(1.00,.56,.99),(.31,.39,.37))
R(cans,"bottle shoulder",.030,(1.00,.56,.99),(1.00,.56,1.045),(.40,.46,.42))
R(cans,"blue cap",.022,(1.00,.56,1.045),(1.00,.56,1.077),(.035,.11,.28))

# Three red handled wall pliers.
tools = asset("hanging pliers")
for i,(x,z) in enumerate([(-.50,1.40),(-.38,1.38),(-.23,1.36)]):
    R(tools,"left handle%d"%i,.010,(x-.045,.661,z-.13),(x-.015,.654,z-.035),red)
    R(tools,"right handle%d"%i,.010,(x+.045,.661,z-.13),(x+.015,.654,z-.035),red)
    R(tools,"left jaw%d"%i,.007,(x-.015,.654,z-.035),(x+.012,.653,z+.06),silver)
    R(tools,"right jaw%d"%i,.007,(x+.015,.654,z-.035),(x-.009,.653,z+.06),silver)
    R(tools,"pivot%d"%i,.014,(x,.645,z-.025),(x,.635,z-.025),gray)

# Foreground wire tangle, separate editable leads.
wires = asset("test leads and loose cables")
for i in range(19):
    cx=random.uniform(-.18,.52)
    cy=random.uniform(-.46,-.17)
    rx=random.uniform(.12,.34)
    ry=random.uniform(.075,.20)
    phase=random.uniform(0,6.28)
    pts=[]
    for j in range(11):

        pts.append((cx+rx*math.cos(t),cy+ry*math.sin(t),
                    .752+.006*(i%4)+.008*math.sin(j*1.1)**2))
    S(wires,"cable%d"%i,pts,.0038,red if i%3==0 else black)
    p=pts[0]
    R(wires,"plug%d"%i,.008,p,(p[0]+.043,p[1]+.014,p[2]+.002),black if i%2 else red)
S(wires,"upright meter red lead",[(.29,.25,.84),(.36,.12,.78),(.47,-.10,.76),(.35,-.36,.77),(.04,-.42,.77)],.004,red)
S(wires,"upright meter black lead",[(.23,.25,.84),(.16,.12,.78),(.12,-.07,.76),(.30,-.30,.77),(.50,-.43,.77)],.004,black)

probes = asset("foreground probes and hand tools")
for i,(x,y,angle,col) in enumerate([
    (.11,-.59,-8,black),(.35,-.56,-18,red),(.52,-.48,35,black),
    (.47,-.19,65,(.03,.14,.45)),(.59,-.21,70,yellow)

    R(probes,"steel point%d"%i,.003,(x+dx,y+dy,.773),(x+dx*1.7,y+dy*1.7,.773),silver)
